summary.title: Unification of the phonon mode behaviour in semiconductor alloys
summary.authors: O. Pagès, M. Kassem, A. Chafi, A. Nassour, S. Doyen, A. V. Postnikov
summary.executive_summary: This paper challenges the traditional classification of phonon mode behavior in semiconductor alloys, which relies on the Virtual Crystal Approximation (VCA) and the Modified Random Element Isodisplacement (MREI) model. The authors argue that this macroscopic description is insufficient and propose a unified percolation-based model operating at the mesoscopic scale. The study focuses on the zincblende alloy ZnTe1-xSex, previously classified as a 'mixed-mode' (2-bond→1-mode) system, and demonstrates that it actually exhibits a '1-bond→2-mode' percolation behavior, similar to In1-xGaxAs and In1-xGaxP. By analyzing Raman and Infrared spectra, the authors identify three distinct transverse optical (TO) modes in ZnTeSe: one Zn-Te mode and a split Zn-Se double-branch corresponding to Se-rich and Te-rich regions. This splitting is attributed to local bond distortions and percolation thresholds. The model is supported by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data for bond lengths and ab initio density functional theory (DFT) calculations using a 32-atom supercell. The results show that the apparent anomalies in the spectra, such as the 'giant' longitudinal optical (LO) mode, arise from strong electric field coupling in the LO symmetry, which masks the underlying 1-bond→2-mode structure visible in the TO symmetry. The paper concludes that the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification is an artifact of this TO/LO duality and that a universal percolation model provides a more accurate description of alloy disorder, offering new insights into mesoscopic self-organization.

claims.description: ZnTeSe exhibits a 1-bond→2-mode percolation behavior, unifying it with InGa alloys.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper challenges the traditional classification of phonon mode behavior in semiconductor alloys, which relies on the Virtual Crystal Approximation (VCA) and the Modified Random Element Isodisplacement (MREI) model. The authors argue that this macroscopic description is insufficient and propose a unified percolation-based model operating at the mesoscopic scale. The study focuses on the zincblende alloy ZnTe1-xSex, previously classified as a 'mixed-mode' (2-bond→1-mode) system, and demonstrates that it actually exhibits a '1-bond→2-mode' percolation behavior, similar to In1-xGaxAs and In1-xGaxP. By analyzing Raman and Infrared spectra, the authors identify three distinct transverse optical (TO) modes in ZnTeSe: one Zn-Te mode and a split Zn-Se double-branch corresponding to Se-rich and Te-rich regions. This splitting is attributed to local bond distortions and percolation thresholds. The model is supported by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data for bond lengths and ab initio density functional theory (DFT) calculations using a 32-atom supercell. The results show that the apparent anomalies in the spectra, such as the 'giant' longitudinal optical (LO) mode, arise from strong electric field coupling in the LO symmetry, which masks the underlying 1-bond→2-mode structure visible in the TO symmetry. The paper concludes that the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification is an artifact of this TO/LO duality and that a universal percolation model provides a more accurate description of alloy disorder, offering new insights into mesoscopic self-organization.

Research Context
The study addresses the challenge of handling substitutional disorder in natural mixtures. A percolation-based approach was previously developed for complex mixtures at the mesoscopic scale. For ideal semiconductor alloys, the virtual crystal approximation (VCA) was traditionally considered sufficient. The VCA views the crystal as a macroscopic continuum with averaged properties. The bond force constant is sensitive to bond distortion and provides insight into disorder. The MREI model supports a classification of TO-Raman/IR data into distinct types. Representative systems include InGaAs, ZnTeSe, and InGaP. The Elliott-CPA criterion predicts type (ii) when optical bands overlap. Previous classifications were found to be inconsistent for certain alloys like InGaP. The authors argue that the VCA misses the essence of phonon behavior.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether the percolation scheme for InGa alloys is universal. The hypothesis is that ZnTeSe obeys the same 1-bond→2-mode percolation behavior. The study aims to extend the percolation model to the ZnTeSe system. It is predicted that ZnTeSe will exhibit a split TO double-branch. The lattice mismatch in ZnTeSe is similar to InGa alloys, suggesting similar distortions. Previous work suggested an analogy between InGaP and ZnTeSe phonon behaviors. The authors propose a three-oscillator version of the percolation model. The model predicts a unique Zn-Te branch and a split Zn-Se branch. The study seeks to unify the traditional MREI-VCA classification into a single class. The percolation model is expected to explain anomalous spectral features.

Methodological Details
The study analyzes Raman and Infrared spectra of ZnTe1-xSex. Representative sets of optical-phonon frequencies were taken from the literature. The data indicate three equally spaced TO modes in the 180–200 cm−1 range. The impurity mode frequencies were estimated using EXAFS measurements of bond length. The shift of impurity modes was inferred from bond length differences. The Gruneisen parameter was used to relate bond length changes to frequency shifts. The splitting parameter was adjusted by fitting a rescaled-MREI curve. Raman lineshapes were calculated using a classical dielectric function. Phonon dampings were scaled like in pure crystals, with a 3:1 ratio. Ab initio calculations used a 32-atom supercell at x~0.5. The plane-wave pseudopotential method within LDA was applied. A linear response technique was used for phonon calculations.

Procedures And Architectures
The percolation model distinguishes vibrations in B-rich and C-rich regions. Each MREI-like TO branch splits into a symmetrical double-branch. Singularities occur at bond percolation thresholds where bonds connect. Below the threshold, finite clusters generate invariance in TO-frequency. Above the threshold, clusters coalesce into a continuum. A rescaled-MREI approach applies to the continuum regime. An ab initio protocol was proposed for data-independent insight. 64-atom supercells were used for the ab initio protocol. The Siesta code was used within the LDA framework. The splitting parameter was estimated from a two-impurity supercell. The systematic error due to LDA was eliminated by this method.

Key Results
The Zn-Te bond exhibits an apparent 1-bond→1-mode MREI behavior. The Zn-Se bond exhibits a well-resolved 1-bond→2-mode behavior. The splitting for the Zn-Se bond was adjusted to ~8 cm−1. The agreement between theoretical curves and data is rather good. A slight discrepancy exists for the Zn-Se branch in the Te-dilute limit. The LO modes exhibit a 'giant' LO+ mode at high frequency. The individual LO modes couple strongly due to the electric field. The presumed unique TO mode is re-assigned as a sum of two modes. The two modes exhibit antagonist strength variations with composition. Ab initio calculations show three equidistant oscillators spaced by ~10 cm−1. A slight overall blue-shift of ~20 cm−1 is due to LDA overbinding. The percolation schemes for InGaAs, InGaP, and ZnTeSe show obvious analogy.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification has no raison d'être. The percolation schemes are consistent with the traditional classifications. The difference in behavior is due to an implicit wrong assumption. TO and LO modes do not behave similarly in an alloy. Strong E-coupling in LO symmetry masks the 1-bond→2-mode behavior. The actual 1-bond→2-mode behavior is visible only in TO symmetry. This TO vs. LO duality explains the previous classification errors. ZnTeSe obeys the 1-bond→2-phonon percolation model. This unifies the classification into a single class. Vibrational spectroscopies provide insight into mesoscopic alloy disorder.

Contradictions And Limitations
The VCA seems sufficient in first approximation but misses the essence. The Elliott-CPA criterion predicts type (ii) for InGaP, but data shows otherwise. The MREI-VCA model cannot account for type (iii) qualitatively. There is a slight discrepancy in the Te-dilute limit for Zn-Se. The LDA method has a well-known overbinding issue. The LO modes are a complicated issue due to multi-wave systems. The model relies on simplified continuum regimes for clarity. The ab initio protocol requires fully-relaxed supercells.

Claims
ZnTeSe exhibits a 1-bond→2-mode percolation behavior, unifying it with InGa alloys. The data indicate three equally spaced TO modes. The Zn-Se bond shows a split double-branch. Ab initio calculations confirm three oscillators. Previous classifications labeled ZnTeSe as type (ii) mixed-mode. The LO modes appear as a single giant mode. The traditional MREI-VCA classification is invalid. Vibrational spectroscopy probes mesoscopic disorder.

Data And Code Availability
The authors acknowledge support from IFCPAR and CINES. The ab initio calculations used the Siesta code.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The ab initio protocol was validated against experimental values. The theoretical and experimental values agree within ~5%. The model forms a self-consistent framework for zincblende alloys.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows schematic views of VCA and percolation approaches. Figure 2 displays TO/LO percolation picture for ZnTeSe. Figure 3 shows calculated TO and LO Raman lineshapes. Figure 4 reproduces simplified percolation schemes for three alloys.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the unification of phonon mode behavior under a percolation model. 2. The strongest evidence is the agreement between ab initio calculations and Raman data. 3. The future path involves studying long-scale self-organization in alloys.
